title: Legionella found in water system of federal building that houses ICE detainees, others
summary: Advocates and state officials are demanding answers on the status of a dangerous bacteria outbreak detected in the water of a Baltimore federal building that houses several agencies, but also a child care facility and an immigration detention center.
content:
by Danielle J. Brown, Maryland Matters March 6, 2026

by Danielle J. Brown, Maryland Matters March 6, 2026

Advocates and state officials are demanding answers on the status of a dangerous bacteria outbreak detected in the water of a Baltimore federal building that houses several agencies, but also a child care facility and an immigration detention center.

Democrats in the state’s congressional delegation sent a letter Friday to General Services Administrator Edward Forst asking what steps had been taken to clear the presence of legionella that was firsst found in the George  H. Fallon Federal Building in November.

“We are particularly concerned by this development in light of reports of overcrowding at the Baltimore Immigration and Customs Enforcement Field Office’s holding rooms, as well as the presence of a child care facility, in the building,” the letter said. “The presence of these bacteria, and the lack of clear direction from GSA, poses a serious health and safety threat for all users of the Fallon Building.”

That building came under fire a few weeks ago, after a video circulated online of an overcrowded ICE detention facility there.

Cathryn Jackson, policy director with the immigrant advocacy group We Are Casa, called the presence of legionella a “damning indictment” of ICE’s “reckless disregard” for those who have been detained for potential immigration violations.

State agencies blast ‘deeply flawed’ ICE detention site, lawmakers want ‘immediate halt’ to project

“Now a potentially deadly bacteria has been found in a building where ICE is detaining people,” Jackson said in a written statement. “That should outrage anyone who believes the government has a basic duty of care to those it locks up. Instead, ICE has repeatedly shown that immigrant lives are treated as disposable.”

Legionella is a bacteria that can spread through water systems and can lead to severe respiratory illness, including pneumonia, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. While most people exposed to the bacteria won’t get sick, certain populations are at a higher risk of severe disease, including smokers, people aged 50 or older and those with specific health conditions such as cancer and diabetes.

Some Maryland state offices in Baltimore faced their own legionella outbreakfrom late 2024 into 2025. Several buildings located at State Center in Baltimore had to shut down for a few days to allow the water system to be flushed out. During thiat time, state employees were instructed to work from home out of an abundance of caution.

A Trump administration spokesperson did not respond to questions about whether the legionella was impacting the ICE facility at the Fallon Building, but did say that GSA is “committed to ensuring the safety of federal employees, contractors, and visitors in our federal buildings.”

A written statement from a GSA spokesperson said that the agency has implemented a plan to clear legionella from the Fallon Building.

“This plan includes documented flushing, temperature and residual disinfectant checks, and periodic retesting for Legionella,” the written statement said. “GSA is communicating regularly with our tenant agencies and ensuring that our facilities are safe for employees and the public.”

But the Maryland lawmakers are concerned that tenants of the Fallon Building have received “varying levels of communication” about the outbreak. They want an update from federal officials about plans to resolve the legionella situation by March 20.

“We must ensure that our federal employees, along with other tenants of and visitors to the building, are being afforded clear communication and a safe working environment,” the letter said.

Meanwhile, Jackson with CASA is pushing for better treatment of the those detained for immigration violations, including undocumented individuals.

“ICE must be held accountable for yet another preventable threat to the health and safety of the people it detains,” Jackson said.
